note: On-demand Linux prices, from the JSON files that AWS's own pricing pages load (published 2026-11-21 for EC2 and EBS, 2026-11-19 for VPC). cost.py reads this table; a run's results record the prices it used.

sources.gp3_gb_month: https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2/USD/current/ebs.json, 'Storage General Purpose gp3 GB Mo' (the data of https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/). The 3,000 IOPS and 125 MB/s that cloud.sh provisions are gp3's included baseline: the file prices only IOPS and throughput above it, and the baseline itself is from AWS's EBS documentation, not from this file.
sources.snapshot_gb_month: https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2/USD/current/ebs.json, 'Storage Snapshot Amazon S3 GB Mo' (the standard tier; the data of https://aws.amazon.com/ebs/pricing/)
sources.public_ipv4_hour: https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/vpc/USD/current/vpc.json, 'Hourly charge for In use Public IPv4 Addresses per Hrs' (the data of https://aws.amazon.com/vpc/pricing/)
sources.data_out_gb: NOT CONFIRMED: AWS's usual first-tier price for data out of us-east-1 to the internet; no machine-readable source was found (the EC2 pricing page's data-transfer file did not load). cost.py counts the bytes collect fetches to this machine at this price, ignoring the 100 GB a month that AWS gives free.

not_counted: Data transfer inside one availability zone over private addresses is free; the EC2 API calls are free.
